work.title: Narratio ad Ammonium de fuga sua sub Juliano

paragraphs.text: But if the one who fears the Lord is blessed — and now we have taken courage to call him blessed, since we have a sure word that he has reached the harbor, as it were, and has a life free of care. If only this might come about for each of us too! If only each of us might finish the race in the same way! If only each of us, as we sail, might bring our own vessel to anchor in the harbor there, untouched by storms, so that, resting with the fathers, we might say, “Here I will dwell, for I have chosen it.” So, beloved and most dearly longed-for brothers, do not weep for Theodore, for he has not died but is sleeping. Let no one shed tears in remembering him; rather, let him emulate his life. For we ought not to grieve over one who has departed to the place where there is no grief. I write this to all of you together, but especially to you, beloved and most dearly longed-for Horsiesius, so that, now that he has fallen asleep, you may take up the whole charge and be to the brothers what he was. For while he was still living, the two of you were like one: when one was away, the other met the needs of both, and when both were present you were as one, speaking to the beloved brothers about what would benefit them. Act in this way, then, and as you do so, write and let us know about your own welfare and that of the brotherhood. And pray, all of you together, I beg you, that the Lord may grant still greater peace to the churches. For even now we have celebrated both Easter and Pentecost with good cheer, and we rejoice in the Lord's benefits. We have written to you. Greet all who fear the Lord. Those with me greet you. I pray that you may be well in the Lord, beloved and most dearly longed-for brothers. Now some time ago, in the presence of my lowly self and of other clergy of the Church of Alexandria, in the Great Church, the blessed Pope Athanasius said something about Theodore to Ammonius of blessed memory, who was bishop of Elearchia, and to Hermon, bishop of Bubastis. I think that your holiness was also present then and heard it, but I am writing down what he said as a reminder to your piety. When the bishops I have mentioned were expressing their admiration for the blessed Antony (for Antony had often met with him), Pope Athanasius said to them: “In these times too I have seen great men of God: Theodore, the sanctified head of the monks of Tabennesi, and the father of the monks around Antinoe, Abba Pammon by name, both of whom fell asleep a short while ago. For when I was being persecuted by Julian and expected to be put to death by him (for it had been made known to me [?] …

… [wish]ing to hide with Theodore, I boarded his boat, which was covered on all sides, and Abba Pammon also came along to escort us. When the wind turned unfavorable, I was praying in anguish of heart, while the monks with Theodore went ashore and towed the boat. And Abba Pammon, comforting me in my anguish, said: “Believe me when I tell you: my heart is not so confident in a time of peace as it is in times of persecution. For I am confident that, suffering for Christ and strengthened by his mercy, even if I am killed, I will find all the more mercy with him.” While I was still saying these things, Theodore looked intently at Abba Pammon and smiled, and when Abba Pammon nearly laughed, I said to them, “Why did you laugh when I said this? Did you condemn me for cowardice?” Theodore said to Abba Pammon, “Tell him why we smiled.” When Abba Pammon replied, “You ought to tell him,” Theodore said: “At this very hour Julian has been killed in Persia. For God had spoken of him beforehand in this way: ‘The drunken man, the scornful, the boastful man, will accomplish nothing [?].’ But a Christian emperor will arise, who will be illustrious, but will live only a short time. Therefore you should not trouble yourself to go off to the Thebaid; rather, go secretly to the imperial court. For you will meet him on the way, and after being sincerely received by him you will return to the Church. And so he will be taken away by God all the sooner.” And so it happened. This is why I believe that many who are pleasing to God remain hidden, especially among the monks. For these men too went unnoticed, as did the blessed Amoun and the holy Theodore on the mountain of Nitria, and the servant of God, the most [?] Pammon … [?]
